answers.ask: What should the course itself look like - bright candy platforms, a neon speed-run aesthetic, or something else? Only the characters were described as anime.
answers.answer: Use a bright, colorful anime-inspired speed-run aesthetic with clean floating platforms and obvious parkour obstacles.

answers.ask: Roughly how many levels should ship in the first build?
answers.answer: Ship 5 course levels for the first build, each requiring more speed and awarding more wins than the last.

scene_prompt: Create a bright, colorful anime-inspired speed-run parkour map with clean floating platforms and obvious obstacles. Arrange five distinct course levels in increasing difficulty, each as a separate elevated route with longer or more demanding parkour sections than the previous level; provide a clear starting area and progression toward the higher-level courses.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, with Obby & Platformer as a secondary genre. The progression-and-upgrade loop makes this a simulator; the secondary genre contributes the visible parkour presentation without changing the simulator-led structure.

### Shape and preset
Use `tier-ladder`, matched from the Stat Grinder preset. Here it is a bright sequence of five visibly ascending anime speed-run course tiers, each one presenting a longer and more demanding elevated route than the last. The preset’s training stations, purchase gates, and rebirth pad are not included because the scene does not describe their geometry.

### Config requirements
Use `obstacle-jump` for clean floating platforms, stepped climbs, long jumps, and obvious parkour obstacles on every course tier. No universal options are implied.

### Layout requirements
No additional placed layout markers are required by the described scene. The five routes and their obstacle geometry are rendered directly rather than represented by invisible placement volumes.

### Layout components
Build one clear starting area at the front and lowest point of the map, with an unobstructed view toward the full progression ladder. Beyond it, arrange exactly five distinct course levels in a readable rising line or broad staircase, each on its own elevated floating-platform route. Level one is the shortest, most welcoming route nearest the start; each subsequent level sits farther back and higher than the previous one, with longer spans, more vertical stepping, and denser or more demanding jumps. Keep all routes visually separate and easy to identify from the start area while preserving a single shared exterior space. Use clean floating platforms, bold obstacle silhouettes, bright color-coded tiers, and minimal decorative clutter so jump paths remain legible. The map is open to the sky, with no enclosing building; the outer boundary is the surrounding open-air void beyond the floating courses. Compose the frame diagonally from the start through all five ascending routes, with the fifth tier forming the highest, most distant focal point.

### Render order
Use `isometric` first and treat it as authoritative, because the scene is a visually led simulator progression set rather than a genre-wide procedurally validated obstacle course.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use a medium scale, driven by the five separate elevated course tiers and their shared start area. Theme: bright, colorful anime-inspired speed-run parkour with crisp floating geometry and highly readable obstacles. Use `tiered` because the five course levels rise in elevation without platforms or floors overlapping above one another; otherwise use `P0`.
